description.narrative: By supporting women – and promoting dialogue among and between them – the programme will seek to ensure that women change agents from all ages and backgrounds work towards a more just, peaceful, and inclusive society.
Formal and informal networks of activists; women's groups; civil society leaders; traditional religious and community leaders; local officials; international and regional actors.

Specific objectives: 1) The women’s movement is more inclusive for creating social change; 2) Traditional gender norms are challenged by new gender values, behaviors, and practices; 3) Women’s participation is more diverse and legitimate in peacebuilding.
This regional programme is part of a broader international programme implemented by a coalition of NGOs lead by PAX.

comment.narrative: It was envisaged that women would receive a higher percentage of representation and increased number of seats in legislative councils by 2022.

Key focus will be surmounting the barriers against women's political leadership pursuits and involvement in political change and peace processes at different levels including pushing for full implementation of laws, policies and strategies and women included in peace groups.

comment.narrative: Established 3 peace groups with 78 women activists and organisations. So far no safe spaces have been created yet.

5 peace groups will be created by the end of the project, to discuss the women's agenda. The safe spaces will be online forums and at grassroots levels in 2022, and transform into joint physical meetings across different peace groups as contexts improve.

comment.narrative: Some safe spaces were already present at grassroots levels to influence political change, shrinking civil spaces rendered most of them inactive.
Activated some existing spaces through 7 regional meetings. In addition, 3 annual meetings will be created depending on the contexts starting from 2023.

comment.narrative: Youth participation is substantial, as many activists are youth themselves. Every peace group has from 3 - 5 youth activists as permanent members. Additionally, youth activists from outisde peace groups are often invited to attend coordinations and discussions. Female participation exceeds that of males. The knowledge on safety and security exists. Additionally peace groups have been trained briefly on digital security. The requirements of the contexts require a higher focus on self care and physical protection.
Solidarity and reflection meetings were hosted for women activists on how to connect with their communities. Activists were connected with lawyers, doctors and other relevant groups.
